newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Five Colombian police linked to murdered Italian.
newsitem.headline: Five Colombian police linked to murdered Italian.

text.p: A Colombian military tribunal ordered the arrest of five policemen on suspicion of taking part in the killing of an Italian tourist in 1995, officials said on Saturday.
The group, two of them officers, are under investigation for the death of student Giacamo Turra while he was in police custody in the Caribbean coast resort of Cartagena in September 1995.
Turra was arrested by a police patrol outside a well-known Chinese restaurant in the colonial port city and died later the same night of multiple internal and external injuries.

The police claimed Turra had been behaving aggressively and was high on drugs. But another man in the police station at the time the Italian was brought in has given evidence in the case, saying that the five patrolmen now under arrest threw Turra down a flight of stairs and repeatedly punched and kicked him.
The tribunal's decision, announced late on Friday, overturns a previous court ruling that failed to find sufficient proof to link the policemen to the Italian's death.

The slow progress of justice in the case has brought sharp criticism from the Italian government, which threatened to push fellow members of the 15-nation European Union to impose trade sanctions on Colombia.

But in comments on Saturday to El Tiempo, Colombia's leading daily, diplomats at the Italian embassy in Bogota said; "We're very satisfied with the tribunal's decision. We hope this positive step is followed by others."
In comments to local media, however, the attorney for the five policemen said his clients were scapegoats in a political tug-of-war between the Colombian and Italian governments.
